cues.text: Welcome to Redox and Electrochemistry.
This recorded Chemistry class uses an AI generated Marin voice.
Oxidation raises oxidation number, while reduction lowers it.
The oxidizing agent accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
The reducing agent supplies electrons and is itself oxidized.
No oxygen atom is required for a redox reaction: zinc can transfer electrons
directly to copper ions.
Oxidation numbers sum to the overall species charge.
An element in its elemental form has oxidation number zero.
Oxygen is usually minus two, but in a peroxide it is minus one.
Hydrogen is usually plus one, but in metal hydrides it is minus one.
Fluorine in its compounds is minus one.
For permanganate, four oxygens contribute minus eight, and the ion's total
charge is minus one.
Manganese must therefore be plus seven.
Reduction to manganese two plus requires five electrons per manganese.
Reduction to manganese dioxide instead ends at plus four and requires three.
The final product fixes the electron count.
In a balanced redox equation, electrons lost equal electrons gained.
Assign oxidation numbers first, identify the two changes, and then use
electron
balance to establish the stoichiometric ratio.
To balance redox half reactions in acidic medium, balance the main element,
oxygen with water, hydrogen with hydrogen ions, and charge with electrons.
For permanganate becoming manganese two plus, place four waters on the product
side, eight hydrogen ions on the reactant side, and five electrons on the
reactant side.
Iron two plus loses one electron to form iron three plus.
Multiply its half reaction by five and add.
The combined equation consumes one permanganate, eight hydrogen ions and five
iron two plus ions.
It produces one manganese two plus, four waters and five iron three plus ions.
Both sides have total charge plus seventeen.
Thus zero point zero two zero zero moles of permanganate require zero point
one
zero zero moles of iron two plus.
In basic medium with manganese dioxide as the specified product, the balanced
reduction consumes one permanganate, two waters and three electrons, forming
one manganese dioxide and four hydroxide ions.
Each side has one manganese, six oxygen and four hydrogen atoms, with charge
minus four.
Zero point zero two zero zero moles now require zero point zero six zero zero
moles of electrons.
Do not copy the acidic five electron count into a reaction with a different
product.
Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance.
Conductivity removes the effect of sample geometry: multiply conductance by
the
cell constant, which is electrode separation divided by area.
Molar conductivity compares conductivity with molar concentration.
With conductivity in siemens per centimetre and concentration in moles per
litre, molar conductivity is one thousand times conductivity divided by
concentration, in siemens centimetres squared per mole.
The factor one thousand comes from the volume unit conversion.
Consider resistance two hundred ohms, cell constant one point two zero per
centimetre, and concentration zero point zero five zero zero molar.
Conductance is zero point zero zero five zero zero siemens.
Conductivity is zero point zero zero six zero zero siemens per centimetre.
Molar conductivity is one hundred twenty siemens centimetres squared per mole.
On dilution, conductivity usually falls because a unit volume contains fewer
ions, while molar conductivity rises as interionic effects decrease and, for
weak electrolytes, ionization increases.
These trends refer to different quantities and are not contradictory.
At infinite dilution, Kohlrausch's law adds the limiting ionic contributions
with their stoichiometric coefficients.
A salt releasing two identical anions contributes that anion term twice.
Always write the units before using a numerical conductivity formula.
A galvanic cell separates oxidation and reduction so electrons can pass
through
an external circuit.
In a Daniell cell, zinc loses electrons at the anode, and copper ions gain
them
at the cathode.
Electrons flow through the wire from zinc to copper.
The salt bridge carries ions that maintain charge balance; electrons do not
travel through its solution.
Anode means oxidation and cathode means reduction in both galvanic and
electrolytic cells.
In a functioning galvanic cell the anode is negative and cathode positive.
An external power supply drives an electrolytic cell, whose electrode
polarities differ, but those reaction based definitions remain.
Cell notation conventionally places the anode on the left and cathode on the
right.
A single line marks a phase boundary, while a double line represents the
electrolyte junction.
Standard reduction potentials are measured relative to a reference electrode,
conventionally the standard hydrogen electrode.
A single isolated electrode potential is not measured without a comparison.
Before calculating voltage, write the oxidation and reduction processes and
balance their electrons.
A correct subtraction formula cannot rescue a reaction whose anode and cathode
were assigned inconsistently.
Using standard reduction potentials, the standard cell voltage equals the
cathode potential minus the anode potential.
Copper two plus to copper has the illustrative value plus zero point three
four
volts, while zinc two plus to zinc has minus zero point seven six.
Their difference is plus one point one zero volts.
Do not multiply electrode potentials when multiplying half reactions to
balance
electrons.
Voltage is an intensive quantity.
Gibbs energy change for the balanced reaction equals minus n times Faraday's
constant times reversible cell voltage.
Here n is two.
With Faraday's constant approximately ninety six thousand five hundred
coulombs
per mole, the standard Gibbs energy change is minus two hundred twelve point
three kilojoules per mole of reaction as written.
Doubling the entire reaction doubles n and the Gibbs energy change, while
leaving voltage unchanged.
Combining this relationship with standard Gibbs energy equals minus R T times
natural log K gives natural log K equals n F times standard voltage divided by
R T.
A positive standard cell voltage therefore implies K greater than one.
At reaction equilibrium the actual voltage is zero, while the standard voltage
need not be zero.
Keep the standard state separate from the present composition.
The Nernst equation corrects the standard voltage for the current mixture.
Cell voltage equals standard voltage minus R T divided by n F, multiplied by
the natural logarithm of the reaction quotient Q.
For a base ten logarithm at approximately two hundred ninety eight kelvin, the
coefficient is about zero point zero five nine one six volts divided by n.
For zinc reacting with copper two plus, Q is approximately zinc ion
concentration divided by copper ion concentration in the ideal dilute model.
Pure solid metals are omitted.
With zinc ions at zero point one zero molar and copper ions at one point zero
molar, Q is zero point one zero.
Its logarithm is minus one.
With n equal to two and standard voltage one point one zero volts, subtracting
the negative correction gives approximately one point one three volts.
In the opposite concentration ratio, Q equal to ten lowers the voltage to
about
one point zero seven volts.
Use dimensionless activities for the rigorous expression, and the stated ideal
approximation for these examples.
At equilibrium, Q equals K and actual reversible voltage is zero.
A concentration cell can have zero standard voltage but a nonzero actual
voltage because its two sides have different activities.
Electrolysis calculations begin with charge, not voltage.
Charge passed is current times time in seconds.
Divide by Faraday's constant to obtain moles of electrons.
Divide again by the electrons required per product particle, then multiply by
molar mass.
Copper two plus requires two electrons to produce one copper atom.
Suppose two point zero zero amperes flow for four thousand eight hundred
twenty
five seconds.
The charge is nine thousand six hundred fifty coulombs.
With Faraday's constant ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole,
this supplies zero point one zero zero moles of electrons and can form zero
point zero five zero zero moles of copper.
Using molar mass sixty three point five grams per mole gives three point one
seven five grams, or three point one eight grams to three significant figures.
That assumes all current produces the desired copper.
At eighty percent current efficiency, multiply by zero point eight zero zero
to
obtain two point five four grams.
Do not divide by the efficiency.
Competing reactions reduce the desired yield for a given charge.
When several cells carry the same charge, each product amount still depends on
its own electron requirement and molar mass.
A primary cell is not designed for normal repeated recharging.
The familiar zinc carbon dry cell uses zinc oxidation and manganese dioxide
cathode chemistry.
Secondary cells are designed for recharging by driving the net chemistry in
reverse.
During lead acid battery discharge, lead is oxidized at the negative electrode
and lead dioxide is reduced at the positive electrode.
Both form lead sulfate.
The net reaction consumes lead, lead dioxide and two sulfuric acid units,
producing two lead sulfate units and two waters.
Acid is consumed during discharge.
The fact that both electrodes form the same sulfate does not mean both were
oxidized: lead changes from zero to plus two, while lead in lead dioxide
changes from plus four to plus two.
Charging reverses the net chemistry with an external energy supply.
A hydrogen oxygen fuel cell receives reactants continuously from outside and
produces water overall.
Two hydrogen molecules combine with one oxygen molecule to form two waters.
Continued operation requires fuel, oxidant and appropriate operating
conditions; it is not unlimited energy.
Distinguish the storage of reactants inside a battery from their external
supply to a fuel cell.
Detailed dry cell mechanisms and electrode classifications remain for further
study.
Conductivity can also estimate how much a weak electrolyte ionizes in a
suitable dilute model.
Divide measured molar conductivity by its limiting molar conductivity to
estimate the ionization fraction alpha.
Suppose a monoprotic acid has molar conductivity twenty and limiting molar
conductivity four hundred, in the same units.
The fraction is zero point zero five zero zero, or five percent.
For starting concentration zero point zero one zero zero molar, the acid
constant is approximately concentration times alpha squared divided by one
minus alpha.
Substitution gives about two point six three times ten to the minus five in
the
conventional concentration model.
Retaining the denominator accounts for the undissociated fraction.
Limiting conductivity may be assembled from limiting ionic contributions using
Kohlrausch's law when direct extrapolation for a weak electrolyte is
unreliable.
This estimate assumes the conductivity ratio is an appropriate measure of
ionization and neglects additional activity effects.
It is not a universal exact acid constant measurement.
Check whether the supplied quantity is conductivity or molar conductivity,
whether the units agree, and whether the concentration is in the required
units.
Use the twelve original quiz questions and seven worked examples to connect
these calculations with cells, redox balance and electrolysis.
Two identical metal electrodes can produce a cell voltage when their ion
activities differ.
Consider zinc electrodes in an ideal dilute model at twenty five degrees
Celsius, with zinc ion concentrations zero point zero zero one zero and zero
point one zero zero molar.
The standard cell voltage is zero because the electrode couples are the same.
The actual voltage is not zero: concentration contributes through the Nernst
equation.
The concentrated compartment acts as the cathode in the spontaneous
orientation, consuming zinc ions by reduction.
The dilute compartment acts as the anode, producing zinc ions by oxidation.
With two electrons transferred, the voltage is zero point zero five nine one
six divided by two, times the base ten logarithm of one hundred, giving zero
point zero five nine one six volt.
The process tends to reduce the concentration difference.
Use activities when nonideality matters, and neglect liquid junction
contributions only within the stated model.
Identical electrode materials therefore do not guarantee identical electrode
potentials.
Label the compartments and electron direction before writing the concentration
ratio, because reversing the cell reverses the voltage sign.
Standard cell voltage connects electrochemistry with both Gibbs energy and the
equilibrium constant.
At twenty five degrees Celsius, the base ten logarithm of the dimensionless
equilibrium constant equals electron number times standard voltage divided by
approximately zero point zero five nine one six volt.
Suppose a defined two electron reaction has standard voltage zero point one
one
eight three two volt.
The logarithm is four and the equilibrium constant is ten thousand.
The corresponding standard Gibbs energy is minus electron number times the
Faraday constant times standard voltage.
Using Faraday constant ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole
gives
about minus twenty two point eight four kilojoules per mole of reaction as
written.
Doubling a reaction doubles the electron count and Gibbs energy change, but it
does not double its electrode voltage.
The equilibrium constant for the doubled equation is squared.
Actual reaction direction also depends on composition through the reaction
quotient.
A positive standard voltage is therefore not a guarantee that every possible
initial mixture operates spontaneously in the written direction.
Keep equation scaling, standard states and actual mixture conditions separate.
Independent ionic migration at infinite dilution allows useful conductance
combinations.
For a weak monoprotic acid H A, combine the limiting molar conductances of
hydrochloric acid and the sodium salt of A, then subtract sodium chloride.
The sodium and chloride contributions cancel, leaving hydrogen ion plus A ion.
With illustrative values four hundred twenty six, ninety one and one hundred
twenty six in compatible conductance units, the result is three hundred ninety
one.
Suppose a zero point zero one zero zero molar acid has conductivity one point
five six four times ten to the minus four siemens per centimetre.
Its molar conductivity is one thousand times conductivity divided by
concentration, or fifteen point six four siemens square centimetres per mole.
Dividing by the limiting value gives an approximate ionized fraction zero
point
zero four zero.
In the simple weak acid model, K a is concentration times alpha squared
divided
by one minus alpha, about one point six seven times ten to the minus five.
This inference assumes the stated dilute solution and ion mobility
approximations; activities, water ionization and other dissolved electrolytes
can require a fuller treatment.
Cells connected in series receive the same charge, but their deposited masses
depend on molar mass and electron stoichiometry.
Take one thousand nine hundred thirty coulombs through a copper two ion cell
and a silver ion cell.
Using Faraday constant ninety six thousand five hundred, the charge
corresponds
to zero point zero two zero zero mole of electrons.
Copper deposition needs two electrons per atom, giving zero point zero one
zero
zero mole of copper.
With illustrative molar mass sixty three point five, the ideal mass is zero
point six three five gram.
Silver requires one electron per atom, giving zero point zero two zero zero
mole and mass two point one five eight grams for molar mass one hundred seven
point nine.
If only eighty percent of charge produces copper, its deposited mass becomes
zero point five zero eight gram.
Do not apply that efficiency to a different cell unless specified.
Equal current and time establish equal charge, not equal moles of deposited
atoms.
Check the actual electrode product and electron number before using the
equivalent mass ratio.
Corrosion can involve different anodic and cathodic regions on a metal
surface.
In a common neutral aerated water model, iron oxidizes to iron two ions while
oxygen is reduced with water to hydroxide ions.
The oxygen half equation consumes four electrons per oxygen molecule and
produces four hydroxide ions.
Two iron oxidation events supply those four electrons.
Further reactions lead to hydrated iron oxide materials commonly called rust;
the complete material is not captured by one simple dissolved ion alone.
A sacrificial zinc coating or connected zinc piece can preferentially oxidize
while electrical contact and suitable environmental conditions are maintained,
helping protect iron.
A tin coating can serve as a barrier, but a damaged coating exposes a
different
galvanic situation and does not provide the same sacrificial protection.
Do not decide behaviour from a coating's appearance alone.
Oxygen supply, moisture, electrical contact and the actual solution affect the
process.
Distinguish prevention by excluding the environment from prevention by
directing oxidation to a more readily oxidized metal.
Standard potential tables are a starting guide, not a substitute for the real
corrosion conditions.
Electrode potentials cannot generally be added like reaction energies.
Consider supplied reduction steps for the same element in one consistent
medium.
The three plus ion accepts one electron to become the two plus ion, with
standard reduction potential plus zero point six zero volt.
The two plus ion accepts two electrons to form the metal, with potential minus
zero point three zero volt.
The overall step transfers three electrons.
Convert each potential to standard Gibbs energy using minus n F E, add the two
energies, then divide by minus three F.
The resulting potential is zero volt, because one times zero point six zero
plus two times minus zero point three zero equals zero.
The simple arithmetic mean would instead give plus zero point one five volt,
which is wrong.
All endpoint states and standard state conventions must match for this
cancellation.
Zero standard potential means zero standard Gibbs energy for the combined half
reaction relative to the chosen reference, not that every actual mixture is at
equilibrium.
Composition can still change the electrode potential.
Disproportionation converts one oxidation state into both a higher and a lower
oxidation state.
Use supplied rounded aqueous copper reduction potentials: copper one plus
accepting one electron to become copper metal has plus zero point five two
volt, and copper two plus accepting one electron to become copper one plus has
plus zero point one five volt.
Reverse the second half reaction to oxidize one copper one plus ion.
Add it to reduction of another copper one plus ion.
The balanced result is two copper one plus ions forming one copper two plus
ion
and one copper atom.
Standard cell potential is zero point five two minus zero point one five, or
plus zero point three seven volt.
One electron transfers per written reaction, so standard Gibbs energy is minus
zero point three seven F.
Positive standard voltage favours disproportionation under the stated standard
conditions.
It does not guarantee the same behaviour in every ligand environment:
complexation, precipitation and activities can alter the comparison.
Check atom balance, charge balance and the electron count before inferring a
redox direction.
A hydrogen electrode is at zero standard potential only under its specified
standard conditions.
Write the reduction as two hydrogen ions plus two electrons forming hydrogen
gas.
At two hundred ninety eight kelvin, with hydrogen pressure equal to the
standard pressure and approximately ideal gas behaviour, the Nernst equation
gives potential minus zero point zero five nine one six times p H in volts
relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.
Thus p H three gives minus zero point one seven seven four eight volt,
while p H five gives minus zero point two nine five eight zero volt.
The potential difference between these otherwise matched electrodes has
magnitude zero point one one eight three two volt.
The lower p H side has the more positive reduction potential and acts as the
cathode in the ideal cell.
This model neglects liquid junction potentials and uses hydrogen ion
activities
through the definition of p H.
A nonstandard gas pressure adds its own term.
Always state temperature, gas pressure and reference before treating a
measured
potential as a p H indicator.
Water electrolysis produces different gas amounts at the two electrodes
because
their electron requirements differ.
In a supplied ideal acidified water model with inert electrodes, the cathode
reduces hydrogen ions to hydrogen, while the anode oxidizes water to oxygen.
Each hydrogen molecule corresponds to two electrons, and each oxygen molecule
to four.
Suppose the same circuit passes nineteen thousand three hundred coulombs,
using
Faraday constant ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole.
The electron amount is zero point two zero zero mole.
At full current efficiency, hydrogen production is zero point one zero zero
mole and oxygen production zero point zero five zero zero mole.
At the same temperature and pressure, with approximately ideal gas behaviour,
their dry volumes are in ratio two to one.
Do not add the electrode electron amounts: the same circuit charge passes
through both electrodes.
Competing electrode reactions, gas dissolution, leakage and collection over
water can change observed amounts or require corrections.
This model specifically excludes chloride or other species that could change
the anode product.
Balance each half reaction before translating charge into a collected gas
amount.
A measured resistance depends on both the liquid and the electrode geometry.
Calibrate the cell with a standard of known conductivity at the stated
temperature.
Suppose the standard conductivity is zero point zero zero one two zero siemens
per centimetre and its measured resistance is one hundred ohms.
Multiplying gives cell constant zero point one two zero per centimetre.
Now put the unknown solution in the same unchanged cell.
A resistance of three hundred ohms gives conductivity zero point zero zero
zero
four zero zero siemens per centimetre.
If its analytical concentration is zero point zero zero two zero zero mole per
litre, multiply conductivity by one thousand and divide by that concentration
to obtain molar conductivity two hundred siemens square centimetres per mole.
Resistance is not simply the reciprocal of conductivity: its reciprocal is
conductance, which still contains geometry.
The factor one thousand converts the litre concentration convention to the
centimetre volume convention.
Keep temperature, immersion geometry and units consistent between calibration
and measurement.
These supplied values illustrate calibration arithmetic rather than certify a
particular commercial reference solution.
Faraday calculations begin with charge, not with a current reading taken at an
arbitrary instant.
Suppose current rises linearly from two amperes to four amperes during six
hundred seconds.
The current time area is a rectangle of twelve hundred coulombs plus a
triangle
of six hundred, giving eighteen hundred coulombs in total.
Equivalently, the average of the two endpoint currents is three amperes for
this linear ramp.
Using the final current for the entire interval would wrongly give twenty four
hundred coulombs.
In a supplied copper deposition model, only eighty percent of the charge
reduces copper two ions to metal; the remainder goes to other electrode
processes.
Copper receives fourteen hundred forty coulombs.
With two electrons per copper atom, Faraday constant ninety six thousand five
hundred coulombs per mole and copper molar mass sixty three point five grams
per mole, the deposited mass is about zero point four seven four gram.
Current efficiency allocates charge, not the number of electrons required by
the copper half reaction.
An endpoint average is exact for this linear ramp, but a general current trace
needs its actual area.
Oxidation numbers determine electron exchange, but they do not finish an
aqueous equation.
In a supplied alkaline model, permanganate is reduced to manganese dioxide
while sulfite is oxidized to sulfate.
Manganese changes from plus seven to plus four, accepting three electrons per
atom.
Sulfur changes from plus four to plus six, losing two electrons per atom.
The smallest shared electron count is six, so use two permanganates and three
sulfites.
Completing the basic half reaction balance and cancelling common water and
hydroxide gives two permanganates, three sulfites and one water forming two
manganese dioxides, three sulfates and two hydroxides.
Each side contains two manganese atoms, three sulfur atoms, eighteen oxygen
atoms and two hydrogens.
Total charge is negative eight on each side.
Thus zero point zero two zero zero mole permanganate corresponds to zero point
zero three zero zero mole sulfite consumed in this stated net conversion.
Do not carry over the five electron acidic permanganate factor: the selected
manganese product is different.
Medium and endpoint species must be specified before assigning the redox
equivalent factor.
Battery capacity in ampere hours is an amount of charge, not an amount of
energy.
One ampere hour equals three thousand six hundred coulombs.
For an ideal lead acid cell discharging by the stated overall reaction, one
mole of lead metal and one mole of lead dioxide consume two moles of sulfuric
acid while two moles of electrons pass through the external circuit.
Thus an ideal one ampere hour discharge corresponds to three thousand six
hundred divided by twice the Faraday constant moles of reaction.
Using ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole gives about zero
point
zero one eight seven mole each of lead and lead dioxide consumed, and zero
point zero three seven three mole sulfuric acid.
The acid is a reactant, not merely an unchanged conducting medium.
These are theoretical stoichiometric amounts for one cell under the stated
discharge model.
Actual usable capacity depends on accessible material, operating conditions
and losses.
To calculate electrical energy, integrate cell voltage against transferred
charge, or use a justified average voltage; an ampere hour rating alone does
not supply that voltage.
The material of an electrode can change the overall electrolysis reaction even
when the cathode deposits the same metal.
Compare two stipulated copper sulfate cells with enough copper ions, complete
copper deposition at the cathode and one thousand nine hundred thirty coulombs
passed.
With Faraday constant ninety six thousand five hundred, each cell transfers
zero point zero two zero zero mole electrons and deposits zero point zero one
zero zero mole copper.
At a copper anode, oxidation dissolves the same copper amount, so the anode
loses zero point six three five gram while the cathode gains that mass for
molar mass sixty three point five.
The ideal bulk copper ion inventory is replenished.
With a suitable inert anode and water oxidation as the only anode reaction,
oxygen production is zero point zero zero five zero zero mole and hydrogen ion
production zero point zero two zero zero mole.
Copper ions are consumed without metal replacement from that anode.
Sulfate is a spectator in this model.
Electrode labels describe oxidation and reduction, not whether the electrode
must always dissolve.
Actual competing reactions, current efficiency and solution composition must
be
checked before applying these ideal inventories.
An aqueous sodium chloride cell contains water as a possible reactant, so its
products need not match molten sodium chloride.
In the stipulated concentrated brine model with suitable electrodes, water
reduction gives hydrogen and hydroxide at the cathode rather than deposition
of
sodium metal.
Chloride oxidation gives chlorine at the anode.
Adding the half equations cancels electrons and yields two chlorides plus two
waters forming one hydrogen molecule, one chlorine molecule and two
hydroxides.
Sodium ions remain counterions.
For zero point one zero zero mole electrons at complete efficiency for those
specified products, hydrogen and chlorine amounts are each zero point zero
five
zero zero mole and hydroxide amount zero point one zero zero mole.
These are separate compartment production amounts before crossover or
secondary
reactions.
Chlorine contacting hydroxide can change the final products, so the simple
ledger assumes effective separation.
The selected anode product depends on concentration, electrode surface and
overpotential; a standard potential table alone does not guarantee chlorine
under every aqueous condition.
This comparison explains a supplied cell's observations and charge balance,
rather than providing a procedure for generating or collecting these reactive
gases.
A fuel cell's reversible electrical work is linked to Gibbs energy, not
automatically to all the heat available from combustion.
Use the supplied standard reaction for one mole hydrogen and half a mole
oxygen
forming one mole liquid water at the stated temperature.
Let the reaction Gibbs change be minus two hundred thirty seven kilojoules per
mole and the enthalpy change minus two hundred eighty six.
Two moles of electrons move through the external circuit per mole hydrogen.
Dividing two hundred thirty seven thousand joules by twice Faraday constant
ninety six thousand five hundred gives a reversible cell voltage of
approximately one point two two eight volts.
On the specified liquid water enthalpy basis, the reversible electrical
efficiency is two hundred thirty seven divided by two hundred eighty six,
approximately eighty two point nine percent.
This does not state that every operating device achieves that efficiency.
Finite current voltage losses, fuel utilization and auxiliary power can reduce
delivered electrical output.
Changing temperature or using water vapour and a different heating value
changes the comparison.
A cell voltage is an energy per charge, while efficiency is a dimensionless
ratio with an explicit energy basis.
A metal electrode responds to the activity of the reacting free ion, not
automatically the total concentration of every complex containing that metal.
Consider silver metal in a stipulated solution at twenty five degrees Celsius,
with total dissolved silver zero point zero one zero zero molar and free
ammonia held at zero point one zero molar.
Use formation constant ten to the seven for the diamminesilver ion, and
neglect
other complexes, precipitation and activity corrections.
Free silver concentration is total silver divided by one plus formation
constant times ammonia squared.
It is therefore approximately ten to the minus seven molar.
For the reduction silver ion plus electron giving silver metal, the Nernst
expression is standard potential plus zero point zero five nine one six times
the logarithm of free silver concentration relative to one molar.
With standard potential zero point eight zero zero volt, the electrode
potential is approximately zero point three eight six volt.
Using the total zero point zero one zero zero molar instead would incorrectly
give about zero point six eight two volt.
Complexation lowers the free ion activity here.
The resulting electrode potential remains relative to the same reference; it
is
not a complete cell voltage without a second electrode.
Faraday's law must use the charge actually assigned to the desired electrode
reaction.
In a supplied cathode ledger, total charge corresponds to zero point zero five
zero mole of electrons.
Assume eighty percent of that charge deposits silver from silver ions, while
the remaining twenty percent makes hydrogen, with no other cathode process.
Silver reduction needs one electron per silver atom.
Its electron allocation is zero point zero four zero mole, so the deposited
silver amount is the same.
Using the supplied rounded molar mass one hundred eight grams per mole gives
four point three two grams of silver.
The hydrogen allocation is zero point zero one zero mole of electrons, and two
electrons are needed per hydrogen molecule, giving zero point zero zero five
zero mole of hydrogen.
The product mole amounts must not simply be assigned an eighty to twenty ratio
because their electron requirements differ.
The two electron allocations, not the product amounts, sum to the total
electron amount.
This is a stipulated current partition, not a prediction from standard
electrode potentials alone.
Current efficiency, reaction selectivity and thermodynamic voltage answer
different questions.
Any additional electrode process would need its own electron ledger.
Selective metal deposition depends on actual reduction potentials.
Use a supporting illustrative model with two hypothetical metals at two
hundred
ninety eight kelvin.
The first metal, labelled M, has singly charged ions and standard potential
zero point six zero zero volt.
The second metal, labelled N, has doubly charged ions and standard potential
zero point three zero four volt.
The second ion activity stays one.
All activities are dimensionless.
Initially the first ion activity is zero point zero one.
Its potential is zero point six zero zero plus zero point zero five nine two
times log zero point zero one, giving zero point four eight one six volt.
It is the more positive couple.
Removing the first metal lowers its dissolved ion activity and potential.
Equality with the second couple occurs when the logarithm of the first ion
activity is minus five.
That first ion activity is ten to the minus five.
This ideal potential comparison excludes overpotential, transport limits,
complexation and solvent reactions; practical separation needs those
additional
checks.
A conductivity minimum during acid base titration does not mean that all ions
vanish.
In a supporting ideal model, titrate fifty milliliters of zero point one zero
zero molar hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide at the same concentration.
Supplied fixed ionic molar conductivities are three hundred fifty for
hydrogen,
fifty for sodium, seventy six for chloride and one hundred ninety eight for
hydroxide.
Their units are siemens multiplied by square centimeters, divided by moles.
Neutralization replaces highly mobile hydrogen ions with less mobile sodium
ions before equivalence.
Chloride remains as a spectator.
Include the changing total volume.
At fifty milliliters of added base, five millimoles of acid have reacted in
one
hundred milliliters total solution.
Sodium and chloride are each zero point zero five zero molar.
Their conductivity contribution is zero point zero zero six three siemens per
centimeter, not zero.
Beyond equivalence, excess hydroxide raises conductivity in this model.
Fixed ionic conductivities are approximate, while measured conductance also
depends on cell geometry.
A cell's voltage variation with temperature can connect electrochemistry to
reaction entropy.
Use the standard reversible cell potential for one specified reaction and its
fixed pressure temperature derivative.
Since standard Gibbs energy is minus n F E, differentiating with respect to
temperature and using the Gibbs entropy relation gives standard reaction
entropy equal to n F times the voltage temperature slope.
This is a supporting thermodynamic extension; it concerns the reversible
standard potential, not an arbitrary loaded terminal voltage.
In a supplied example at three hundred kelvin, let electron number be two,
Faraday constant ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole, standard
voltage zero point three zero zero volt, and slope minus zero point zero zero
zero two zero volt per kelvin.
Standard Gibbs energy is minus fifty seven point nine kilojoules per mole of
the written reaction.
Standard entropy is minus thirty eight point six joules per mole kelvin.
Adding T times that entropy to Gibbs energy gives standard enthalpy minus
sixty
nine point four eight kilojoules per mole.
Convert entropy to consistent energy units before combining.
A falling voltage therefore indicates negative reaction entropy in this
comparison, not automatically a nonspontaneous reaction.
